entry.title: Plage du Kelenn, Carantec
entry.summary: Plage du Kelenn is a sheltered sand beach in Carantec, on a bay of small islands near Roscoff. The tide goes out very far, leaving wide flats of firm sand, and the church spire and low granite houses give the bay its look.

entry.title: Plage de Mimizan
entry.summary: Mimizan has a wide Atlantic beach of fine sand backed by high dunes and pine forest. The surf is strong enough for surf schools, and a cycle path runs through the pine woods behind the dunes.

entry.title: Plage du Trez, Benodet
entry.summary: Plage du Trez is a long curve of fine sand in Benodet, on the south coast of Brittany, with a grassy bank and a promenade behind it. The bay is mild and sheltered, and the town has a harbour, a lighthouse and boat trips to the Glenan islands.

entry.title: Plage de Trestraou, Perros-Guirec
entry.summary: Trestraou is the main beach of Perros-Guirec, a wide curve of fine sand on the Pink Granite Coast, with a sea-front promenade and a view of the offshore islands. The tide range is large, so the beach changes between low and high water.

entry.title: Praia dos Olhos de Agua
entry.summary: Olhos de Agua is a small fishing village with a golden beach framed by red cliffs and rock outcrops. The name refers to freshwater springs that bubble up through the sand at low tide, and the beach continues east into the long Praia da Falesia.

entry.title: Vila Nova de Milfontes Beach
entry.summary: Vila Nova de Milfontes is a white village at the mouth of the River Mira on the Alentejo coast. Sheltered river beaches sit beside open Atlantic beaches, with dunes, dry scrub and cliffs along the coast path, in the Southwest Alentejo and Vicentine Coast Natural Park.

entry.title: Praia da Barra, Aveiro
entry.summary: Praia da Barra is a wide Atlantic beach of golden sand beside the striped lighthouse of Aveiro, the tallest in Portugal. The sea is open Atlantic, so waves and wind are common, and the beach is popular with surfers and kite-flyers.

entry.title: Praia Grande, Ferragudo
entry.summary: Praia Grande is a wide beach of golden sand beside the fishing village of Ferragudo, at the mouth of the Arade river opposite Portimao. A small castle guards the river mouth, and the sea is calm and shallow near the shore.

entry.title: Playa Paraiso, Villajoyosa
entry.summary: Playa Paraiso is a wide beach of pale sand in Villajoyosa, with palms along the back and clear turquoise water. The old town of colourful houses is a short walk away, and the region is known for its chocolate.

entry.title: Playa de Regla, Chipiona
entry.summary: Playa de Regla is a wide beach of fine sand in Chipiona, with the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Regla standing behind it. The nearby lighthouse is the tallest in Spain, and the tide goes out far, leaving long firm flats of sand.

entry.title: Playa de Islantilla
entry.summary: Islantilla is a long, quiet beach of golden sand on the Huelva coast, with low dunes, pine woods and golf courses behind. The tide goes out a long way, leaving wide flats of firm sand, and the sea is calmer than on the open coast further east.

entry.title: Playa de Matalascanas
entry.summary: Matalascanas is a long Atlantic beach of golden sand at the edge of Donana National Park. A strange rock stands in the sea, the Tapon, and the wide beach has dunes and pine woods behind it. The sea is open Atlantic, so waves can be strong.

entry.title: Opatija Beach
entry.summary: Opatija is the grandest Habsburg resort on the Adriatic, with swimming from stone platforms, small pebble coves and bathing piers along the Lungomare promenade. Villas and parks climb the green hillside behind, and the sea is clear and deep.

entry.title: Lovran Beach
entry.summary: Lovran is an old Habsburg seaside resort on the Kvarner coast, with a small pebble beach along a long stone promenade. Villas and parks line the shore, laurel woods rise behind, and the sea is clear and deep close to the edge.

entry.title: Bilin Zal Beach, Lumbarda
entry.summary: Bilin Zal is a shallow cove of sand and fine pebbles near the village of Lumbarda at the eastern end of Korcula. The water is clear and calm, and the island is known for its vineyards and for its sandy beaches, which are rare on this coast.

entry.title: Baska Voda Beach
entry.summary: Baska Voda is a small Dalmatian town on the Makarska Riviera, with a long pebble beach lined by pines and palms and the high Biokovo mountains rising behind. The water is clear and shelves gently, and the promenade is lively in summer.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Fontane Bianche
entry.summary: Fontane Bianche is a seaside village south of Syracuse, with a long beach of soft pale sand and clear turquoise water. The sea is shallow and calm, and the beach is popular with Sicilian families in summer.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Portonovo
entry.summary: Portonovo is a bay of white pebbles and clear blue water below the green cliffs of the Conero headland. A small medieval church and a Napoleonic fort stand behind the beach, and the setting is one of the finest on the Adriatic coast.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Velluto, Senigallia
entry.summary: Senigallia is known for its Spiaggia di Velluto, the velvet beach, a very wide stretch of fine soft sand with shallow water. The Rotonda a Mare pier stands out in the sea, and the old town is a short walk from the shore.

entry.title: Spiaggia del Poetto, Cagliari
entry.summary: Poetto is the long city beach of Cagliari, a wide band of pale sand running for several kilometres beneath the rocky headland of the Sella del Diavolo. The water is shallow and clear, and beach bars and a promenade keep it lively in summer.

entry.title: Glystra Beach, Rhodes
entry.summary: Glystra is a small, quiet cove on the Lardos coast of Rhodes, with fine sand and pebbles and clear blue water below dry scrub hills. It is a short drive from the busier resorts and usually calm in the morning.

entry.title: Marmari Beach, Kos
entry.summary: Marmari is a long, wide beach of fine sand on the north coast of Kos, backed by low dunes and tamarisk trees. A steady breeze keeps the heat down and brings small waves, so it suits swimmers and windsurfers.

entry.title: Stegna Beach, Rhodes
entry.summary: Stegna is a small bay of sand and fine pebbles on the east coast of Rhodes, sheltered by a rocky headland. The water is clear and calm, and the village behind has a handful of tavernas and a relaxed feel.

entry.title: Agnontas Beach, Skopelos
entry.summary: Agnontas is a small fishing hamlet on a narrow green bay on the south-west coast of Skopelos. A pebble beach lies at the head of the bay, with pine-covered hills on both sides and calm, clear water.

entry.title: Skala Beach, Kefalonia
entry.summary: Skala is a long, gently shelving beach of golden sand and fine pebbles on the south coast of Kefalonia. Pine woods run down behind the shore, the water is clear, and the long beach leaves plenty of space even in summer.

entry.title: Playa de la Victoria, Cadiz
entry.summary: Playa de la Victoria is a long beach of fine golden sand stretching along the modern side of Cadiz, with a wide promenade and Atlantic waves. It is a lively city beach, and the old town and cathedral are a short walk or bus ride away.

entry.title: Selce Beach, Crikvenica
entry.summary: Selce is a small resort on the Kvarner coast between Crikvenica and Novi Vinodolski, with pebble beaches, calm water and green pine-covered hills behind. The sea is clear, and the long promenade links the beaches in both directions.

entry.title: Playa de La Herradura
entry.summary: La Herradura is a horseshoe-shaped bay of grey pebbles and coarse sand on the Costa Tropical of Granada, with steep green hills behind and clear blue water. It is a quiet, local resort with a small marina and good diving nearby.

entry.title: Plage de Soulac-sur-Mer
entry.summary: Soulac-sur-Mer is a seaside town at the tip of the Medoc with a wide beach of fine sand and traditional striped beach tents. The Atlantic is cool, and swimming is supervised by lifeguards in summer.

entry.title: Stavros Beach, Crete
entry.summary: Stavros is a small, sheltered bay of fine sand and clear shallow water on the Akrotiri peninsula of Crete. A rocky hill rises behind the beach, and the film Zorba the Greek was shot here.
